query: Invent a genuinely new primitive for moving information between distant positions in a million-token sequence. It must not be a variant of softmax attention, of kernelised or linear attention, of a state-space or gated linear recurrence, of long convolutions, of block or top-k sparse selection over a stored key-value cache, or of retrieval into an external index. Name it, and give its per-token time and memory as explicit functions of sequence length. Name the three published systems it sits closest to and one mechanistic difference from each. State one falsifiable quantitative claim and the benchmark you would test it on, and one regime where it should lose to ordinary attention.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Novelty is scored ONLY against this list; every entry carries a resolvable identifier and the year of FIRST publication of the concept (not of any later rebranding).
Softmax dot-product self-attention, the reference primitive (arXiv:1706.03762, 2017).

Fixed sparse / strided / windowed / global attention patterns: Sparse Transformers (arXiv:1904.10509, 2019), Longformer (arXiv:2004.05150, 2020), BigBird (arXiv:2007.14062, 2020), sliding-window as shipped in Mistral 7B (arXiv:2310.06825, 2023).
Low-rank and random-feature approximations of the attention matrix: Linformer (arXiv:2006.04768, 2020), Performer (arXiv:2009.14794, 2020).
Hash/bucket-based approximate attention: Reformer LSH attention (arXiv:2001.04451, 2020).

Linear attention as an RNN with matrix-valued state (arXiv:2006.16236, 2020). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: the underlying outer-product fast-weight memory is Schmidhuber's fast-weight controller (doi:10.1162/neco.1992.4.1.131, 1992); the equivalence is made explicit in arXiv:2102.11174 (2021).

Structured state-space sequence models and their gated/selective successors: S4 (arXiv:2111.00396, 2021), Mamba (arXiv:2312.00752, 2023), Griffin gated linear recurrence + local attention (arXiv:2402.19427, 2024), MiniMax-01 lightning attention (arXiv:2501.08313, 2025).

Gated / delta-rule linear recurrences: RWKV (arXiv:2305.13048, 2023), RetNet (arXiv:2307.08621, 2023), Gated Linear Attention (arXiv:2312.06635, 2023), parallel DeltaNet (arXiv:2406.06484, 2024), Gated DeltaNet (arXiv:2412.06464, 2024), log-linear attention (arXiv:2506.04761, 2025).

Implicit long-convolution and token-mixing operators: Hyena (arXiv:2302.10866, 2023), Monarch Mixer (arXiv:2310.12109, 2023), FNet Fourier mixing (arXiv:2105.03824, 2021), MLP-Mixer (arXiv:2105.01601, 2021).

Associative / content-addressable memory as the mixing operator: product-key memory layers (arXiv:1907.05242, 2019), Memory Layers at Scale (arXiv:2412.09764, 2024), and the attention-equivalent continuous Hopfield layer (arXiv:2008.02217, 2020). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: the associative-memory concept is Hopfield (doi:10.1073/pnas.79.8.2554, 1982) and dense associative memory is Krotov and Hopfield (arXiv:1606.01164, 2016); 2020 is the transformer-attention equivalence, not the concept.

Segment-recurrent and compressive carry-over of past activations: Transformer-XL (arXiv:1901.02860, 2019), Compressive Transformer (arXiv:1911.05507, 2019), Recurrent Memory Transformer (arXiv:2207.06881, 2022), Infini-attention (arXiv:2404.07143, 2024).

kNN / landmark retrieval folded into the attention operator: Memorizing Transformers (arXiv:2203.08913, 2022), Landmark Attention (arXiv:2305.16300, 2023), retrieval-augmented generation over an external index (arXiv:2005.11401, 2020).

Learned, natively trainable sparse selection over the KV cache: Native Sparse Attention (arXiv:2502.11089, 2025), MoBA block attention (arXiv:2502.13189, 2025), and the trade-off study in The Sparse Frontier (arXiv:2504.17768, 2025).
Fast weights updated by an inner learning loop at test time as the sequence mixer: TTT layers (arXiv:2407.04620, 2024), Titans neural long-term memory (arXiv:2501.00663, first posted 31 Dec 2024).
Latent-bottleneck cross-attention that decouples cost from input length: Perceiver (arXiv:2103.03206, 2021).
External differentiable memory with learned read/write heads: Neural Turing Machines (arXiv:1410.5401, 2014), Differentiable Neural Computer (doi:10.1038/nature20101, 2016).

KV-side capacity reductions that change what is stored per position: multi-query attention (arXiv:1911.02150, 2019), grouped-query attention (arXiv:2305.13245, 2023), multi-head latent attention (arXiv:2405.04434, 2024).
Positional-encoding schemes that extend range without changing the mixing operator: RoPE (arXiv:2104.09864, 2021), ALiBi (arXiv:2108.12409, 2021).

Exact-attention systems reformulations (same math, different IO/parallelism): FlashAttention (arXiv:2205.14135, 2022), Ring Attention (arXiv:2310.01889, 2023), PagedAttention (doi:10.1145/3600006.3613165, 2023).
The recall-versus-throughput trade-off result that constrains any constant-state design, plus the hybrid it motivates (arXiv:2402.18668, 2024).
Measurement conventions for long-context claims: RULER (arXiv:2404.06654, 2024), long-context data engineering to 128k (arXiv:2402.10171, 2024).

Hierarchical / multi-resolution mixing that summarises the sequence at coarser scales: Funnel-Transformer (arXiv:2006.03236, 2020), H-Transformer-1D hierarchical-matrix attention (arXiv:2107.11906, 2021), Hourglass hierarchical transformers (arXiv:2110.13711, 2021), multi-resolution-analysis attention (arXiv:2207.10284, 2022), MEGABYTE multiscale patching (arXiv:2305.07185, 2023). Fast-multipole-style hierarchical summarisation over positions is covered here.

Learned reordering, clustering, or permutation that brings distant positions adjacent before mixing: Routing Transformer (arXiv:2003.05997, 2020), Sparse Sinkhorn Attention (arXiv:2002.11296, 2020), Nystromformer landmark approximation (arXiv:2102.03902, 2021).

Global mixing by iterating to a fixed point rather than by an explicit pairwise operator: Deep Equilibrium Models (arXiv:1909.01377, 2019); Universal Transformers as weight-tied depth recurrence (arXiv:1807.03819, 2018).
Block-level recurrence carrying a state across chunks: Block-Recurrent Transformers (arXiv:2203.07852, 2022).
hard_rules: Gives the primitive an explicit name AND states per-token time cost and per-token memory cost as formulas in the sequence length n (both formulas must be present).

The defining operation is not softmax attention, kernelised/linear attention, a linear state-space or gated linear recurrence, a long convolution, block or top-k sparse selection over a stored KV cache, or retrieval into an external index; naming these for contrast is allowed, building on them as the core mechanism is not.
Names at least three specific published systems or papers as nearest prior art and states one concrete mechanistic difference from each.
States at least one falsifiable quantitative claim containing a numeral and names the benchmark, dataset, or measurement used to test it.
States at least one regime, sequence length, or task family in which the primitive is expected to be worse than exact softmax attention.
expert_baseline: Competent experts converge on framing commitments rather than a device: per-token cost must be constant or near-constant in sequence length, some lossy compression of the distant past is unavoidable, and long-range quality is bounded by how many bits the retained state holds, so the design question is where to spend a fixed state budget. The expected response therefore argues from the recall-versus-throughput trade-off, fixes an explicit state size, specifies read and write costs separately, is honest that exact recall over 1M tokens cannot be bought with a constant state, and validates on synthetic needle-style and aggregation-style long-context suites at 128k to 1M tokens before claiming any win over exact attention. Note that the specific fix most experts reach for first, a constant-size recurrent state plus a local exact-attention window, is itself prior art here and is excluded by this item's own constraints.

query: High-quality human text is running out and training on model output degrades the distribution. Invent a genuinely new source of learning pressure for a frontier pretraining run: not more scraped or licensed human text, not imitation of model-generated text however filtered, not reinforcement learning against a verifier, judge, or preference model, and not self-play in a game with a known win condition. Name it. Say exactly where the new information physically comes from and why it is not a recycling of what the model already knows. Give a quantitative claim you would test at a stated token or compute scale, name the diagnostic you would use to detect distributional collapse and the reading of it that would show your proposal failing, and state the cost or throughput of acquiring the signal with an explicit magnitude and unit, arguing whether it reaches pretraining scale.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Novelty is scored ONLY against this list; every entry carries a resolvable identifier and the year of FIRST publication of the concept (not of any later rebranding).
Compute-optimal scaling and the data budget it implies: Kaplan scaling laws (arXiv:2001.08361, 2020), Chinchilla (arXiv:2203.15556, 2022).

The human-text ceiling itself: Will we run out of data? (arXiv:2211.04325, 2022) and the follow-on projection Can AI scaling continue through 2030 (https://epoch.ai/blog/can-ai-scaling-continue-through-2030, 2024).
Data-constrained scaling by repeating epochs and mixing in code (arXiv:2305.16264, 2023).

Model collapse from recursive training on generated data: The Curse of Recursion (arXiv:2305.17493, 2023); later journal version doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07566-y (2024). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: 2023, not the 2024 Nature date; and the degradation-from-model-output effect was already reported in 2022 by Data Feedback Loops (arXiv:2209.03942, 2022) and Will Large-scale Generative Models Corrupt Future Datasets? (arXiv:2211.08095, 2022).

Self-consuming generative loops and their stability: MAD loops (arXiv:2307.01850, 2023), stability of iterative retraining (arXiv:2310.00429, 2023), collapse as a change of scaling laws (arXiv:2402.07043, 2024), statistical analysis of synthetic-data training (arXiv:2404.05090, 2024).

Accumulating rather than replacing real data as a collapse fix (arXiv:2404.01413, 2024); Collapse or Thrive? mixing-ratio study (arXiv:2410.16713, 2024); sample-selection bias as a collapse driver (arXiv:2606.13732, 2026).

Verification as the escape hatch from collapse: Beyond Model Collapse (arXiv:2406.07515, 2024), Escaping Model Collapse via Synthetic Data Verification (arXiv:2510.16657, 2025), contraction-conditioned neural filters (arXiv:2512.00757, 2025).

Model-generated instruction and preference corpora: Self-Instruct (arXiv:2212.10560, 2022), Evol-Instruct/WizardLM (arXiv:2304.12244, 2023), Nemotron-4 340B synthetic-data pipeline (arXiv:2406.11704, 2024).
Curated or rewritten synthetic pretraining corpora: Textbooks Are All You Need (arXiv:2306.11644, 2023), Rephrasing the Web (arXiv:2401.16380, 2024).
Bootstrapped self-generated reasoning traces filtered by correctness: STaR (arXiv:2203.14465, 2022), Quiet-STaR (arXiv:2403.09629, 2024).
AI feedback and self-scoring as the training signal: Constitutional AI (arXiv:2212.08073, 2022), RLAIF (arXiv:2309.00267, 2023), Self-Rewarding Language Models (arXiv:2401.10020, 2024).
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards at scale: Tulu 3 (arXiv:2411.15124, 2024), DeepSeek-R1 (arXiv:2501.12948, 2025).

Self-play against a known win condition or formal checker: AlphaZero (doi:10.1126/science.aar6404, 2018), AlphaGeometry (doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06747-5, 2024), Absolute Zero self-proposed tasks (arXiv:2505.03335, 2025).

Human preference and demonstration data as the marginal signal: fine-tuning from human preferences (arXiv:1909.08593, 2019), learning to summarize (arXiv:2009.01325, 2020), HH-RLHF (arXiv:2204.05862, 2022), DPO (arXiv:2305.18290, 2023).
Interaction with a live external environment as the data source: WebGPT browsing with human feedback (arXiv:2112.09332, 2021), test-time RL on unlabelled streams (arXiv:2504.16084, 2025).

Widening the corpus to non-text modalities and scientific sequence data: Llama 3 data mix (arXiv:2407.21783, 2024); pretraining on the human reference genome, HyenaDNA (arXiv:2306.15794, 2023). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: HyenaDNA is a model trained on an existing genomic corpus, not a new corpus.
Paying data generators as a supply-side mechanism rather than a new signal type (arXiv:2601.09966, 2026).
Physical and embodied instrumentation as the data source: pooled robot-fleet teleoperation and execution data, Open X-Embodiment (arXiv:2310.08864, 2023).

Automated experimentation that manufactures new ground truth rather than reusing text: the Robot Scientist (doi:10.1038/nature02236, 2004; doi:10.1126/science.1165620, 2009), the A-Lab autonomous synthesis laboratory (doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06734-w, 2023), Coscientist LLM-driven autonomous chemistry (doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06792-0, 2023).

Choosing which measurement to make so as to maximise expected information gain: Bayesian experimental design, Lindley (doi:10.1214/aoms/1177728069, 1956) and the review by Chaloner and Verdinelli (doi:10.1214/ss/1177009939, 1995).
Logged deployment interaction as a learning signal rather than as text: counterfactual reasoning and learning from logged bandit feedback (arXiv:1209.2355, 2012).
hard_rules: Names the signal AND identifies its information source as a specific named external process, instrument, or population, distinct from the model's own outputs.

The core signal is not additional scraped or licensed human text, imitation of model-generated text, reinforcement learning against a verifier / judge / preference model, or self-play with a known win condition; contrasting with these is allowed.
States a quantitative claim containing a numeral and an explicit token count, parameter count, FLOP budget, or dollar budget at which it would be tested.
Names a specific diagnostic for distributional collapse or diversity loss and states what reading of it would show the proposal failing.

States the acquisition cost or throughput of the signal with an explicit magnitude and unit (tokens per day, dollars per million tokens, sensor-hours, or participant-hours) and argues whether that reaches pretraining scale.
expert_baseline: The convergent expert position is that the binding constraint is information, not tokens: repeated epochs buy little, purely self-generated corpora contract the tails of the distribution, and any durable fix must inject information from outside the model. Experts agree that some external verification or grounding channel must anchor each new datum, that real data must be retained rather than replaced, that diversity metrics and tail coverage must be tracked generation over generation, and that the proposal only matters if the channel is cheap and parallel enough to deliver a pretraining-scale volume rather than a fine-tuning-scale one.

query: Consider a model more competent than any available human reviewer on the tasks it is deployed for, where no human can check its work end to end. Invent a genuinely new oversight artifact that yields a trustworthy training or approval signal. It must not be debate between models, task decomposition or amplification of a weak overseer, a critique or verifier model scoring outputs, weak-to-strong training, probing or interpretability tooling on internal activations, or reading the chain of thought. Name it. State the single assumption that makes it sound and what breaks it. Say who or what supplies ground truth and at what cost. Describe the smallest experiment that could demonstrate it today - task domain, capability gap, success criterion - and what a misaligned model would do to defeat it.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Novelty is scored ONLY against this list; every entry carries a resolvable identifier and the year of FIRST publication of the concept (not of any later rebranding).
Learning a reward model from human preference comparisons (arXiv:1706.03741, 2017); recursive reward modelling as the scaling story (arXiv:1811.07871, 2018).

Iterated amplification / factored cognition: supervising strong learners by amplifying weak experts (arXiv:1810.08575, 2018); book-length recursive decomposition in practice (arXiv:2109.10862, 2021); factored cognition inside a control setting (arXiv:2512.02157, 2025).

Debate: AI safety via debate (arXiv:1805.00899, 2018); the obfuscated-arguments obstruction (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/PJLABqQ962hZEqhdB/debate-update-obfuscated-arguments-problem, 2020); doubly-efficient debate (arXiv:2311.14125, 2023); empirical debate with unreliable or weak judges (arXiv:2311.08702, 2023; arXiv:2402.06782, 2024; arXiv:2407.04622, 2024).
Critique and self-critique models that assist human evaluators (arXiv:2206.05802, 2022); recursive self-critiquing for superhuman oversight (arXiv:2502.04675, 2025).

Sandwiching methodology for measuring oversight progress with non-expert humans (arXiv:2211.03540, 2022); partitioned human supervision (arXiv:2510.22500, 2025). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: sandwiching was proposed in Cotra, The case for aligning narrowly superhuman models (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/PZtsoaoSLpKjjbMqM/the-case-for-aligning-narrowly-superhuman-models, 5 March 2021); the 2022 paper is the first empirical study, not the origin.
Weak-to-strong generalization: eliciting strong capabilities from weak supervision (arXiv:2312.09390, 2023).

Written-principle and model-generated feedback pipelines: Constitutional AI (arXiv:2212.08073, 2022), RLAIF (arXiv:2309.00267, 2023), rule-based rewards (arXiv:2411.01111, 2024), deliberative alignment (arXiv:2412.16339, 2024) and its stress test (arXiv:2509.15541, 2025).

Legibility as a training target: prover-verifier games (arXiv:2407.13692, 2024). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: the prover-verifier game formulation is Anil et al., Learning to Give Checkable Answers with Prover-Verifier Games (arXiv:2108.12099, 2021); 2024 is the LLM legibility application.
Process supervision over steps rather than outcomes (arXiv:2305.20050, 2023).
Chain-of-thought monitoring and its fragility (arXiv:2503.11926, 2025; arXiv:2507.11473, 2025); bootstrapped monitoring with transparent-reasoning intermediates (arXiv:2606.11998, 2026).
AI control: protocols that stay safe despite intentional subversion, using trusted weak models plus a human audit budget (arXiv:2312.06942, 2023).

Eliciting latent knowledge as a problem statement (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WwsnJQstPq91_Yh-Ch2XRL8H_EpsnjrC1dwZXR37PC8/edit, 2021) and unsupervised or quirky-model probes for it (arXiv:2212.03827, 2022; arXiv:2312.01037, 2023).

AI safety via market making, where a trader and a predictor are trained against each other on a human's eventual judgement (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/YWwzccGbcHMJMpT45/ai-safety-via-market-making, 2020).
Evaluation-centred oversight: model evaluation for extreme risks (arXiv:2305.15324, 2023), dangerous-capability evaluations (arXiv:2403.13793, 2024), structured safety cases (arXiv:2403.10462, 2024).

Failure modes any protocol must survive: sandbagging / strategic underperformance (arXiv:2406.07358, 2024), alignment faking (arXiv:2412.14093, 2024), reward tampering escalation (arXiv:2406.10162, 2024).
Concrete problems framing of scalable supervision (arXiv:1606.06565, 2016).

Mechanism design for eliciting truthful reports when no ground truth is available to the principal: the peer-prediction method (doi:10.1287/mnsc.1050.0379, 2005); Bayesian truth serum (doi:10.1126/science.1102081, 2004). Scoring several independent agents against each other's reports, or against a predicted-consensus term, falls here.

Label-free evaluation of models whose answers no human can check, by testing logical or arithmetic consistency across related queries: Evaluating Superhuman Models with Consistency Checks (arXiv:2306.09983, 2023).
Requiring the system to emit a machine-checkable certificate, proof, or world-model-relative guarantee alongside its output: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI (arXiv:2405.06624, 2024).

Control-protocol machinery an oversight artifact would be composed with: resampling and incrimination protocols, Ctrl-Z (arXiv:2504.10374, 2025); sabotage and sandbagging capability evaluations (arXiv:2410.21514, 2024).
hard_rules: Names the artifact AND states the single assumption that makes it sound as an explicit assumption claim, plus at least one condition under which that assumption fails.

The core mechanism is not model-versus-model debate, task decomposition/amplification of a weak overseer, a critique or verifier model scoring outputs, weak-to-strong training, activation probing or interpretability tooling, or chain-of-thought reading; contrasting with these is allowed.
Identifies who or what supplies ground truth and states its cost in explicit units (human-hours, dollars, wall-clock delay, or fraction of episodes audited).
Describes a minimal demonstration experiment naming a task domain, the capability gap between overseer and overseen, and a measurable success criterion.
States at least one concrete strategy an adversarially misaligned model would use against the artifact, and whether the artifact still holds under it.
expert_baseline: Experts converge on a shared frame rather than a single device: oversight must not require the human to reproduce the work, so it must rest on some asymmetry in which checking, cross-examining, or catching a rare defection is cheaper than doing the task. The expected response accepts a scarce audit budget, assumes verification is easier than generation in the target domain, insists the protocol degrade gracefully when the model knows the protocol, and demands an empirical sandwiching-style demonstration with a real capability gap plus an explicit account of collusion and of the tasks where no checkable asymmetry exists.

query: In reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, models keep finding behaviours that satisfy the grader without doing the task, and teams usually discover it afterwards by reading transcripts. Invent a genuinely new artifact that makes reward hacking visible while the training run is still going. It must not be a better reward model or an ensemble of them, a stronger or adversarial verifier, a monitor that reads the chain of thought, a KL or entropy penalty or other conservative-optimisation trick, or post-hoc transcript review. Name it. Define precisely what quantity it measures and how that measurement is obtained inside the training loop, state its compute overhead as a numeric fraction or multiple of the training step cost, give the numeric signature that would flag a hack, say what you do about false alarms, and name a class of hack it cannot catch.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Novelty is scored ONLY against this list; every entry carries a resolvable identifier and the year of FIRST publication of the concept (not of any later rebranding).

Reward hacking and specification gaming as a named problem: Concrete Problems in AI Safety (arXiv:1606.06565, 2016); the running specification-gaming examples list, first published by Krakovna (https://vkrakovna.wordpress.com/2018/04/02/specification-gaming-examples-in-ai/, 2 April 2018) and later restated on the DeepMind blog (https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/specification-gaming-the-flip-side-of-ai-ingenuity/, 2020). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: the list is 2018, not 2020.

Measurement corruption as a general law: Campbell's law (doi:10.1016/0149-7189(79)90048-X, 1979); Categorizing Variants of Goodhart's Law (arXiv:1803.04585, 2018); Goodhart's Law in Reinforcement Learning (arXiv:2310.09144, 2023).

Formal definitions and measurement of the phenomenon: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking (arXiv:2209.13085, 2022); effects of reward misspecification and phase transitions in it (arXiv:2201.03544, 2022).
Proxy-versus-gold divergence as the canonical detector: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization (arXiv:2210.10760, 2022).
Ensemble and averaging defences: reward-model ensembles (arXiv:2310.02743, 2023); WARM weight-averaged reward models (arXiv:2401.12187, 2024).
Disentangling a known hackable confound from true quality: ODIN length-decorrelated reward (arXiv:2402.07319, 2024).

Step-level supervision as a hack-resistant signal: process- and outcome-based feedback (arXiv:2211.14275, 2022); Let's Verify Step by Step (arXiv:2305.20050, 2023); automatic process supervision (arXiv:2312.08935, 2023). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: process supervision is 2022, not 2023.
Rule-grounded and rubric-grounded rewards, and their own hackability: rule-based rewards (arXiv:2411.01111, 2024); reproducing and detecting hacking in rubric-based RL (arXiv:2606.04923, 2026).

Designing the objective so optimisation pressure is bounded: inverse reward design (arXiv:1711.02827, 2017); quantilizers (https://intelligence.org/files/QuantilizersSaferAlternative.pdf, 2015); attainable-utility preservation (arXiv:1902.09725, 2019).

Behavioural signatures documented in deployed pipelines: sycophancy from model-written evaluations (arXiv:2212.09251, 2022) and its characterisation (arXiv:2310.13548, 2023); reward tampering escalation (arXiv:2406.10162, 2024); emergent misalignment from narrow finetuning (arXiv:2502.17424, 2025).
Chain-of-thought monitoring during RL and the obfuscation it induces when optimised against (arXiv:2503.11926, 2025); monitorability as a fragile property (arXiv:2507.11473, 2025).

Verifiable-reward-specific failures: Spurious Rewards in RLVR (arXiv:2506.10947, 2025); LLMs gaming verifiers (arXiv:2604.15149, 2026); survey of mechanisms in the large-model era (arXiv:2604.13602, 2026).

Training-dynamics and parameter-space detectors: gradient-fingerprint detection and suppression of reward hacking (arXiv:2604.16242, 2026); learned proxy-reward internalisation as a precursor signal (arXiv:2606.09711, 2026).

Structural limits of preference-based training: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of RLHF (arXiv:2307.15217, 2023); DPO's implicit reward view (arXiv:2305.18290, 2023); reward modelling design survey for reasoning RL (arXiv:2602.09305, 2026).
The RLVR pipelines in which this failure now occurs: Tulu 3 (arXiv:2411.15124, 2024), DeepSeek-R1 (arXiv:2501.12948, 2025).

Flagging outputs produced by an unusual internal mechanism rather than by unusual behaviour: mechanistic anomaly detection (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/vwt3wKXWaCvqZyF74/mechanistic-anomaly-detection-and-elk, 25 November 2022) and its empirical test on quirky models (arXiv:2504.08812, 2025).

Planted, deliberately exploitable, or held-out probe tasks used as tripwires, and internals-based deception detection on them: Poser (arXiv:2405.05466, 2024); sabotage evaluations (arXiv:2410.21514, 2024); auditing language models for hidden objectives (arXiv:2503.10965, 2025).
Attributing a reward or behaviour change back to the responsible training data or update: influence functions for black-box predictions (arXiv:1703.04730, 2017).
hard_rules: Names the artifact AND defines the measured quantity precisely, as a formula or as an explicitly specified observable with units.
States where in the training loop the measurement is computed and gives its overhead as a numeric fraction or multiple of the training step cost.

The mechanism is not a reward model or ensemble of reward models, a stronger or adversarial verifier, a chain-of-thought-reading monitor, a KL/entropy/conservative-optimisation penalty, or post-hoc transcript review; contrasting with these is allowed.
States a numeric threshold, trend, or signature that triggers the alarm AND says what happens on a false positive.
Names at least one class of reward hacking the artifact provably or plausibly cannot detect.
expert_baseline: The convergent expert view is that hacking is diagnosed by divergence: a proxy score that keeps climbing while an independent estimate of true task success stalls or falls. Experts therefore expect a trusted held-out probe set scored periodically during the run, tracking of disagreement between graders and of drift away from the reference policy, sample inspection at checkpoints, and early stopping when the gap opens. They also agree the detector must not itself become an optimisation target, that any detector is only as good as its trusted signal, and that overhead must stay small enough to run every few hundred steps.

query: Every static benchmark eventually leaks into training data, and the usual fixes - private held-out sets, post-cutoff refreshes, paraphrase detection, live human preference arenas - decay or get more expensive each cycle. Invent a genuinely new evaluation artifact whose validity does not depend on any item being unseen: something whose score means the same thing after all its contents are public, and whose validity does not rest on secrecy or on being newer than the model. Name it. State the quantity it estimates and the property that makes leakage irrelevant. Describe the comparison you would run to demonstrate that property empirically, naming the statistic you would report and the result that would prove it broken. Give the cost of evaluating one model, and two capability classes it cannot measure.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Novelty is scored ONLY against this list; every entry carries a resolvable identifier and the year of FIRST publication of the concept (not of any later rebranding).
Canary strings and the request not to train on the benchmark: BIG-bench (arXiv:2206.04615, 2022).

Contamination as a measured quantity, and detectors for it: the case for per-benchmark contamination measurement (arXiv:2310.18018, 2023); Min-K% membership detection (arXiv:2310.16789, 2023); rephrased-sample contamination that evades n-gram checks (arXiv:2311.04850, 2023); benchmark-cheating survey (arXiv:2311.01964, 2023).
Human-and-model-in-the-loop adversarial data collection that refreshes items: Adversarial NLI (arXiv:1910.14599, 2019); Dynabench (arXiv:2104.14337, 2021).

Procedural / template / graph-generated items with fresh instances per run: DyVal (arXiv:2309.17167, 2023); functional benchmarks that re-instantiate the same reasoning at new surface values (arXiv:2402.19450, 2024); fresh parallel re-collection of an existing benchmark, GSM1k (arXiv:2405.00332, 2024); fine-grained automatic benchmark generation (arXiv:2605.18824, 2026).

Continuously refreshed, post-cutoff-dated item streams: LiveBench (arXiv:2406.19314, 2024); LiveCodeBench with per-problem release dates (arXiv:2403.07974, 2024); contamination-resistant benchmark construction (arXiv:2505.08389, 2025); static-to-dynamic evaluation survey (https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.511/, 2025).

Execution- and repository-grounded tasks where the grader is a test suite: SWE-bench (arXiv:2310.06770, 2023; https://www.swebench.com/); GAIA assistant tasks with unambiguous answers (arXiv:2311.12983, 2023).

Hard private or expert-authored item pools: FrontierMath (arXiv:2411.04872, 2024); Humanity's Last Exam (arXiv:2501.14249, 2025); private leaderboards run by a third party (https://scale.com/leaderboard, 2024).
Abstraction/generalisation-first designs with held-out private splits: On the Measure of Intelligence and ARC (arXiv:1911.01547, 2019); ARC-AGI-2 (https://arcprize.org/arc-agi/2/, 2025).
Live human preference comparison as the scoring instrument: Chatbot Arena (arXiv:2403.04132, 2024; https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard); LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench (arXiv:2306.05685, 2023).
Interactive, interviewer-style protocols that generate the probe during evaluation: LLM-as-an-Interviewer (arXiv:2412.10424, 2024).
Automatic, declarative construction of new difficult datasets: AutoBencher (arXiv:2407.08351, 2024); model-written evaluations (arXiv:2212.09251, 2022).
Multi-metric standardised evaluation frameworks: HELM (arXiv:2211.09110, 2022); long-context stress suites such as RULER (arXiv:2404.06654, 2024).

Psychometric item-level modelling and adaptive administration, imported into LLM evaluation: Weiss on adaptive testing (doi:10.1177/014662168200600408, 1982); item-response-theory-based benchmark subsampling, tinyBenchmarks (arXiv:2402.14992, 2024); efficient benchmarking (arXiv:2308.11696, 2023). CONCEPT DATE NOTE: item response theory and tailored testing predate the 1982 review; see Lord, Applications of Item Response Theory to Practical Testing Problems, 1980 (doi:10.4324/9780203056615). Item parameters, ability estimates on a common latent scale, and item banking are all pre-1982.
The underlying measurement pathology: Campbell's law on corruption of any social indicator under pressure (doi:10.1016/0149-7189(79)90048-X, 1979).
Elicitation confounds that any leakage-proof design must still handle: strategic underperformance on evaluations (arXiv:2406.07358, 2024).
Fixing a generator and a distribution instead of an item list, so that publishing everything leaks nothing: procedurally generated benchmark environments, ProcGen (arXiv:1912.01588, 2019).

Scoring against outcomes that do not exist yet at answering time, with a fully public question set: ForecastBench (arXiv:2409.19839, 2024); calibration and proper scoring rules as the grading instrument.

Measuring compression or likelihood on fresh text rather than item accuracy: Language Modeling Is Compression (arXiv:2309.10668, 2023); Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly (arXiv:2404.09937, 2024).
Label-free scoring by internal consistency across related queries, which needs no held-out answer key: Evaluating Superhuman Models with Consistency Checks (arXiv:2306.09983, 2023).
Measuring marginal human uplift in a randomised trial rather than model-only accuracy (arXiv:2507.09089, 2025).
hard_rules: Names the artifact AND states in one sentence the quantity it estimates.
States the property that makes leakage irrelevant in a checkable form; that property must not be item secrecy, a private held-out split, or items being newer than the model under test.

Describes an empirical demonstration with an explicit comparison condition (for example deliberately contaminated versus clean models) and names the statistic used, plus the result that would falsify the leakage-invariance claim.
Gives the cost of evaluating one model as a numeral with units (dollars, GPU-hours, or human-hours).
Names at least two capability classes the artifact cannot measure.
expert_baseline: Experts converge on the diagnosis and on the evaluation hygiene, not on a new instrument: any fixed item pool has a finite shelf life, memorisation and true capability are only separable when something varies that memorisation cannot track, and validity claims must be demonstrated by contrast rather than asserted. The expected response fixes a task distribution rather than a task list, insists on machine-checkable grading, and validates by comparing matched contaminated and clean conditions on the same distribution, while conceding that scores drift as models improve and that open-ended qualities remain outside anything auto-generated. Note that the reflexes of dating items or refreshing them after the model's cutoff are excluded by this item's own constraints, so they do not count as a response.
